findings.problem: The contract assumes that a PostgreSQL receipt-guard transaction can keep revocation/takeover totally ordered with SQLite durability even when the PostgreSQL guard session is lost after admission. Session loss releases PostgreSQL locks independently of the SQLite transaction; the SQLite transaction can still reach durable commit after those locks are released. No durable cross-resource admission/fence state or other mechanism closes that interval, so TC-05's deterministic claim that guard loss before SQLite durability always rolls back with proof of no write is not implementable from the stated protocol.
findings.harm: A later authority mutation or Issue #78 takeover can become visible after the PostgreSQL lock disappears while the already-admitted old operation can still commit its first SQLite effect. That violates the claimed provider-acceptance ordering and can permit a stale generation/provider effect after fencing.
findings.required_change: Replace the session-liveness assumption with an implementable durable admission/fencing protocol. At minimum, persist an admission state/witness that survives PostgreSQL-session loss and that later mutation/takeover must honor until provider-first resolution; classify post-admission guard loss as receipt-possible rather than proof-no-write unless an actually atomic provider-side fence proves rollback. Update AC-06/07/09 and TC-04/05 consistently without implementing #78 reconciliation in #77.

findings.problem: TC-01 changes each mutable authority/reference fact before authorize_and_issue_dispatch, but the only concurrent linearization race in TC-02 is an epoch-advancing revocation. The suite therefore does not prove that capability, binding, policy-selector and reference-key mutations themselves participate in the same epoch-lock protocol during permit issuance. An implementation could accidentally omit the epoch serialization from one of those mutation paths while still passing both current tests.
findings.harm: A material capability/binding/policy/reference change could commit concurrently with permit construction and recreate the authority_permit_linearization_gap for mutation classes other than the tested revocation path.
findings.required_change: Make the issuance race parameterized over every mutation class named by AC-03, including Workspace/resource/execution authorization, capability/binding/policy selector and reference-key mutation. For each, prove mutation-first denies or issuance-first binds the exact witnessed prior epoch, with no intermediate stale permit.

findings.problem: AC-04 requires authorize_and_issue_dispatch to sample fresh PostgreSQL clock_timestamp after its blocking execution/epoch locks and reject an expired owner/lease, but TC-03 exercises delayed provider admission rather than permit issuance across expiry. TC-02 races mutation/issuers without forcing the permit transaction to block across its deadline. The contract therefore lacks a deterministic oracle that distinguishes post-lock clock_timestamp from a transaction-start timestamp at permit issuance.
findings.harm: Permit issuance could incorrectly use now()/transaction-start time after lock blocking, minting a permit whose lease was already expired while still satisfying the current provider-deadline tests.
findings.required_change: Add a required permit-issuance test that blocks authorize_and_issue_dispatch on its canonical locks across the lease deadline, skews non-PostgreSQL clocks, then proves fresh post-lock clock_timestamp rejects issuance with no permit/audit dispatch authority.

findings.problem: AC-08 requires observation/finalization to re-establish the current generation-1 owner and a fresh PostgreSQL-time lease, but no required test delays observation or finalization across lease expiry and proves refusal. TC-03 tests provider receipt expiry and TC-08 tests outcome mappings, so an implementation could omit or use the wrong time source for the finalization lease check without violating their stated oracles.
findings.harm: A stale generation-1 owner could finalize ToolActionStore state after its authority lease has expired, creating application state that falsely claims authority over a provider outcome.
findings.required_change: Add an explicit observation/finalization expiry oracle using post-lock PostgreSQL time. Delay a direct or closed provider outcome across lease expiry and prove the stale owner cannot finalize or rewrite provider truth; the lifecycle must remain in the recovery-required state defined by the contract.

findings.problem: TC-04 still requires racing a 'fenced generation change', while DD-05 and out_of_scope assign takeover and generation 2+ to Issue #78 and the invariants explicitly forbid introducing a generation-2 fixture. A generation change from the sole generation-1 owner necessarily exercises generation 2+ semantics or an equivalent fixture, so the required test conflicts with the ticket's own scope boundary.
findings.harm: Implementers must either leak takeover/generation-2 machinery into #77 to satisfy TC-04 or weaken/fake the test, defeating the intended Issue #77/#78 separation and reopening the prior stale_generation_seam_scope concern.
findings.required_change: Remove the generation-change race from #77 acceptance and keep TC-04 limited to epoch mutation and generation-1 receipt fencing that can be exercised without a generation-2 fixture. Preserve the protocol compatibility requirement for later takeover, but require the actual generation-change race in Issue #78 acceptance.

findings.problem: AC-01 states that each pre-acquisition Workspace/resource authorization, ExecutionAuthorizer, exact-compatibility or m4r1 denial creates no execution and makes zero provider calls, but the required cases begin after AcquireApplied or exercise later application/provider outcomes. No deterministic test explicitly covers those fail-fast denial paths or proves absence of an execution row alongside zero gateway calls.
findings.harm: A denied request could accidentally materialize execution/audit state or reach the gateway before acquisition while all existing required cases still pass.
findings.required_change: Add a required application-facing test matrix for every pre-acquisition denial class. Assert no execution is created, no dispatch permit exists, gateway/provider call count is zero, and the public workflow remains the single application-facing write entry point.

findings.problem: AC-10 enumerates the exact information that append-only audit must reconstruct, but TC-09 only says that 'epoch/audit' reconstruct independently and TC-06 focuses on secret/raw-identifier exposure. None of the stated oracles requires reconstructing and comparing the complete actor, both current decisions, exact compatibility, authority witness, lease/permit times, provider identity, immutable intent, observations and outcome set.
findings.harm: Acceptance evidence could show that audit rows survive restart while still omitting one or more security-relevant decision inputs needed to explain why a write was authorized and what provider outcome occurred.
findings.required_change: Add an exact canonical audit-projection oracle that reconstructs every AC-10 field from append-only records after restart and compares it to the execution/permit/provider evidence, while separately asserting absence of secrets and raw provider identifiers.

summary: Revision v4 materially improves authority-epoch permit issuance and PostgreSQL-time receipt admission, but it is not approvable under the supplied rule that any Critical, Major or Minor gap requires rejection. Most importantly, the post-admission PostgreSQL guard-loss case has no implementable atomic ordering relationship with an independent SQLite commit, so the claimed proof-no-write and takeover/revocation ordering can fail. Additional required-oracle and scope gaps remain around non-revocation epoch mutations, permit-issuance expiry, finalization lease expiry, the reintroduced generation-change test, pre-acquisition denials and complete audit reconstruction. Review standard applied from the packet: sufficiency/internal consistency/implementability and mandatory rejection when any gap remains.
